prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

Title, set largest at the top left of the page: compose
Deck beneath it: A scanned book's text and pictures, rescued separately, rejoin here by page number and leave as chapters.

Hero: a long collating table runs across the middle of the page. On it lies a stream of tall text pages in order, each with a small numbered tab at its corner — 9, 10, 11, 12. Above the table sits an open ledger labeled manifest.yaml, its two visible columns listing pictures by page and chapters by page. From the ledger, thin leader lines drop small rectangular picture plates down onto the table, each plate landing beside the page that bears its number. One stray plate follows a gently curving line back to an earlier page and tucks in behind it, with a small note nearby: a picture whose own page vanished joins the last page before it.

At the right end of the table the stream divides. Pages are gathered at each chapter boundary and slid into standing folders — three lean in a row, labeled ch01, ch02, ch03 — and ahead of them a thinner folder holds the unclaimed opening pages, labeled Front Matter. A small note at the first boundary: a chapter begins wherever the ledger says its first page falls.

Two quiet insets along the bottom:
Lower left, a single page magnified: its paragraph text sits above and a small picture plate is tucked beneath, captioned — each page's pictures follow its text, in the order they were cut from the scan.
Lower right, the top edge of a chapter's first page: a duplicate shouted title line lifts away from the sheet, captioned — the chapter title is set once; repeated title lines left over from the scan fall away.

One warm accent colour belongs to the picture plates and the paths they travel; the text pages stay in ink. The ledger, the stream of pages, and the folders share one continuous scene.
